title: Monthly sea-level steps gave no clear pooled time-order asymmetry at 125 gauges in 1960-2024
abstract: We tested whether monthly sea-level rises and falls have different cubic weight after removal of season and trend. In a fixed PSMSL snapshot, 125 well-covered gauges in 1960-2024 gave a normalized third increment moment of -0.01397. Equal weight for 37 occupied geographic cells gave a conditional 95% three-year block interval of -0.05701 to +0.02867. All nine planned checks also had intervals that included zero. This gives no clear pooled time-order asymmetry for this statistic. It does not show reversible ocean dynamics or equal recovery times. The intervals hold the fitted seasonal cycle and trend fixed. Uneven gauge coverage, station changes, gaps and long climate dependence limit inference. The package includes code, aggregate results, draws, source hashes, a figure and an independent numerical audit. Raw source data remain external.

display.caption: Cell-weighted third step moments and conditional 95% year-block intervals. All intervals include zero. The checks use different supports, trends, step limits or time lags.
